articles.headline: Cinco empresas se alían para llevar el primer cable de datos submarino a Galicia
articles.subtitle: El proyecto conectará la costa gallega con una red troncal de fibra óptica capaz de mover grandes volúmenes de información por tres vías simultáneas: terrestre, transoceánica y satelital.
articles.body:
Un consorcio de cinco empresas ha anunciado un proyecto para instalar el primer cable de datos submarino de Galicia, una infraestructura que pretende situar la comunidad en el mapa global de las telecomunicaciones.

La iniciativa contempla el tendido de un cable de fibra óptica que enlazará la costa gallega con redes troncales internacionales, ofreciendo tres rutas de comunicación: una red terrestre, conexiones transoceánicas y enlaces satelitales. El objetivo es reducir la dependencia gallega de los nodos de Madrid y Barcelona para el tráfico de datos.

## El contexto

La carencia de un cable submarino propio ha sido históricamente un lastre para la economía digital de Galicia, obligando a empresas e instituciones a canalizar su tráfico a través de infraestructuras del centro peninsular. El nuevo cable permitiría una latencia significativamente menor y mayor resiliencia frente a cortes.

El proyecto se encuentra en fase de captación de inversores y permisos, y las empresas implicadas esperan tener la primera fase operativa en un plazo de entre 18 y 24 meses. La Xunta de Galicia ha mostrado su apoyo a la iniciativa, que considera estratégica para la diversificación económica de la comunidad.

articles.headline: La intermodal de Lugo y la Praza Conde Fontao siguen sin fecha de apertura
articles.subtitle: Las obras de la estación intermodal y la plaza anexa acumulan meses de retraso mientras los vecinos denuncian la falta de puntos accesibles para personas con movilidad reducida.
articles.body:
La estación intermodal de Lugo y la reforma de la Praza Conde Fontao continúan sin una fecha de apertura definitiva, pese a que los plazos iniciales preveían su finalización para la primavera de este año.

La intermodal, que debía integrar los servicios de autobús urbano e interurbano con la estación de tren, acumula retrasos que el Concello atribuye a problemas con los suministros y a la necesidad de realizar ajustes en el proyecto original.

## Barreras de accesibilidad

Vecinos y asociaciones de personas con discapacidad han denunciado que la plaza carece de puntos accesibles suficientes para sillas de ruedas. Las rampas instaladas en algunos accesos no cumplen con la pendiente máxima recomendada, y faltan pasos de peatones adaptados en varios cruces.

El gobierno local se ha comprometido a revisar el proyecto para corregir las deficiencias antes de la inauguración, pero no ha concretado una nueva fecha. La oposición municipal ha criticado la falta de transparencia en la gestión de las obras.

articles.headline: Detenido un hombre en Lugo por amenazar a una mujer con un cuchillo para robarle
articles.subtitle: La víctima denunció que una desconocida la abordó en la calle, le dijo que le había tocado la lotería, y la amenazó para que sacara dinero de un cajero.
articles.body:
La Policía Nacional de Lugo investiga a un hombre como presunto autor de un robo con intimidación ocurrido en el centro de la ciudad, después de que una mujer denunciara que fue amenazada con un cuchillo y obligada a sacar dinero de su cuenta bancaria.

Según el relato de la víctima, una desconocida la abordó en la vía pública y le dijo que le había tocado un premio de lotería, pidiéndole ayuda para cobrarlo. Cuando la mujer accedió a acompañarla, la conductora de un vehículo que las esperaba cerca la amenazó con un cuchillo y la obligó a extraer efectivo de un cajero automático.

La Policía investiga si se trata de un timo elaborado o de un robo violento, y no descarta que haya más víctimas. Los agentes han pedido colaboración ciudadana para identificar a los sospechosos, que podrían haber actuado siguiendo un patrón similar en otras ciudades gallegas.

articles.headline: Tres incendios en Baltar y Rodeiro queman 135 hectáreas en el sur de Galicia
articles.subtitle: El fuego, que sigue activo en varias zonas, ha obligado a movilizar a medios aéreos y terrestres de la Xunta y del Ministerio, en una jornada de alto riesgo por las altas temperaturas.
articles.body:
Tres incendios forestales declarados en los municipios orensanos de Baltar y Rodeiro han calcinado unas 135 hectáreas, según el último balance de la Consellería do Medio Rural. El fuego más grave se registró en la parroquia de Baltar, donde las llamas avanzaron rápidamente empujadas por el viento y las altas temperaturas.

Medios aéreos y terrestres de la Xunta y del Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica trabajan en la extinción desde el sábado. La BRIF de Laza y varios helicópteros han realizado descargas continuas para contener el avance del fuego, que ha afectado a masa forestal y matorral.

Las autoridades no han informado de daños personales ni de la necesidad de desalojar viviendas, aunque el operativo se mantiene en alerta ante la posibilidad de que el viento reactive las llamas. La Xunta ha recordado que el riesgo de incendios sigue siendo extremo en la mayor parte de Galicia debido a la sequía acumulada.

articles.headline: Así luce Mondoñedo en su mercado más medieval: la villa se vuelca con la recreación histórica
articles.subtitle: Decenas de puestos, espectáculos y talleres transforman el casco histórico de Mondoñedo en un escenario vivo del medievo, en una cita que atrae a visitantes de toda la provincia.
articles.body:
La localidad lucense de Mondoñedo ha celebrado su mercado medieval anual, transformando las calles del casco histórico en un escenario que recrea la vida de la Edad Media. Decenas de puestos de artesanía, alimentación y espectáculos callejeros han atraído a visitantes de toda la provincia y del resto de Galicia.

El mercado, que se ha consolidado como una de las citas estivales más populares de la comarca de A Mariña, incluye este año novedades como talleres de herrería, cetrería y tiro con arco. Los organizadores destacan la implicación de los vecinos, muchos de ellos ataviados con vestimenta de época.

## Impacto turístico

El evento genera un importante impacto económico en la zona, con una ocupación hotelera que roza el cien por cien durante el fin de semana. La alcaldesa de Mondoñedo ha valorado positivamente la afluencia de público y ha avanzado que el ayuntamiento trabaja ya en la edición del próximo año, con el objetivo de ampliar la oferta de actividades.

articles.headline: Las comunidades religiosas de Ceuta se concentran para reclamar una respuesta a la crisis migratoria
articles.subtitle: Manifestantes de todas las confesiones acusan al Gobierno de "abandono" mientras Italia califica de "desproporcionada" la reacción de Sánchez al restablecer los controles fronterizos.
articles.body:
Las comunidades religiosas de Ceuta han convocado una concentración conjunta para reclamar al Gobierno una respuesta urgente a la crisis migratoria desatada tras la entrada masiva de unos 78.000 migrantes desde Marruecos a finales de julio. Los manifestantes, que representan a las confesiones católica, musulmana, hindú y judía de la ciudad, denuncian "abandono" por parte del Estado y reclaman que "Ceuta es España".

La protesta coincide con la escalada diplomática entre España e Italia. El Gobierno de Pedro Sánchez activó el sábado controles fronterizos para viajeros procedentes de Italia después de que Roma se negara a retirar sus propias restricciones, impuestas tras la avalancha migratoria. Italia calificó la medida de "incomprensible y totalmente inaceptable".

## La Marcha Azul y las fisuras en la UE

La denominada Marcha Azul —la entrada masiva organizada de migrantes— ha evidenciado las grietas en la política migratoria europea. El escritor Tahar Ben Jelloun ha señalado en declaraciones a El País que "no entiende por qué se dejó pasar a los jóvenes", sugiriendo que Marruecos utilizó la crisis como herramienta de presión política en un contexto de tensión bilateral.

Marruecos, por su parte, ha negado cualquier responsabilidad en los hechos, mientras que el presidente de la FIFA, Gianni Infantino, ha vinculado la crisis con la geopolítica del fútbol y la candidatura marroquí al Mundial de 2030.

articles.headline: El incendio de Niebla (Huelva) mantiene a 467 personas desalojadas tras arrasar 8.000 hectáreas
articles.subtitle: La noche ha sido "algo más favorable" según la Junta de Andalucía, pero el fuego sigue activo y las labores de extinción se centran en proteger el perímetro de las viviendas aún amenazadas.
articles.body:
El incendio forestal declarado en el municipio onubense de Niebla continúa activo tras varios días sin control, con un balance provisional de 8.000 hectáreas calcinadas y 467 personas desalojadas de sus viviendas. La Junta de Andalucía ha informado de que "la noche ha sido un poco más favorable que las jornadas anteriores, aunque la situación sigue siendo complicada".

El fuego, que ha sido calificado como "de sexta generación" por los expertos —un incendio de una intensidad y comportamiento que supera la capacidad de extinción convencional—, avanza impulsado por las altas temperaturas, la baja humedad y el viento.

## El dispositivo de extinción

Más de 300 efectivos del Plan Infoca, apoyados por la Unidad Militar de Emergencias (UME) y medios aéreos del Ministerio, trabajan en la extinción. Las evacuaciones preventivas han afectado a varias aldeas y núcleos rurales dispersos en el entorno del Parque Natural de Doñana.

La Junta ha habilitado albergues para los desalojados y ha recomendado a la población de las zonas cercanas que permanezca atenta a las indicaciones de las autoridades. La calidad del aire se ha visto afectada en un radio de varios kilómetros, con concentraciones elevadas de partículas en suspensión.

articles.headline: El escritor marroquí Tahar Ben Jelloun: "No sé por qué se dejó pasar a los jóvenes. Faltó inteligencia política"
articles.subtitle: El autor franco-marroquí cuestiona la falta de previsión de las autoridades españolas y marroquíes ante la avalancha migratoria que colapsó Ceuta a finales de julio.
articles.body:
El escritor Tahar Ben Jelloun ha cargado contra la falta de "inteligencia política" de ambos lados de la frontera ante la crisis migratoria de Ceuta, en una entrevista publicada por El País. "No sé por qué se dejó pasar a decenas de miles de jóvenes", afirma el autor, que sugiere que Marruecos "tiene la policía más potente del Magreb" y que la ausencia de respuesta indica una decisión política.

Ben Jelloun, premio Goncourt y una de las voces más respetadas del panorama cultural marroquí, señala que Marruecos ha utilizado históricamente la presión migratoria como herramienta de negociación con España y la UE, pero que en esta ocasión la magnitud del movimiento "no tiene precedentes".

## El papel de Marruecos

Según el escritor, las relaciones bilaterales atraviesan uno de sus momentos más delicados desde la crisis diplomática de 2022. Marruecos esperaba gestos concretos de España respecto al Sáhara Occidental, mientras que el Gobierno de Pedro Sánchez considera que el cumplimiento de los acuerdos migratorios es condición indispensable para cualquier avance.

La crisis ha provocado también un terremoto político interno en España, con la oposición exigiendo explicaciones al Gobierno y la Unión Europea tratando de mediar sin ofrecer soluciones concretas.

articles.headline: Fergie Chambers, el activista millonario detenido en Ibiza que reclama Trump
articles.subtitle: El Gobierno español deberá decidir si extradita a Estados Unidos a este activista propalestino, detenido en Ibiza a petición de la Administración Trump, que lo acusa de financiar el terrorismo.
articles.body:
James Chambers, conocido como Fergie Chambers, el activista millonario estadounidense detenido en Ibiza a principios de agosto, se enfrenta a un proceso de extradición solicitado por el Gobierno de Donald Trump. La defensa de Chambers, encabezada por el exjuez Baltasar Garzón, denuncia una "persecución política" del presidente estadounidense por su apoyo a la causa palestina.

Chambers, de 54 años, es un inversor y filántropo que ha financiado organizaciones de derechos humanos en Oriente Próximo. La Administración Trump lo acusa de canalizar fondos a grupos vinculados con Hamás, algo que él niega rotundamente.

## El dilema del Gobierno español

La decisión final corresponde al Consejo de Ministros, que deberá valorar si los cargos que presenta Estados Unidos tienen suficiente base jurídica o si, por el contrario, existe un componente político que justifique denegar la extradición. La Audiencia Nacional ya ha tomado declaración a Chambers y ha decretado prisión provisional.

El caso tiene una dimensión diplomática delicada, en un momento en que las relaciones entre España y Estados Unidos ya están tensas por las políticas migratorias y comerciales de Trump.

articles.headline: Daniel Kinahan appears in Dublin court after extradition from UAE
articles.subtitle: The alleged Kinahan cartel boss was flown back to Ireland on a government jet and charged with directing the activities of a criminal organisation before the Special Criminal Court.
articles.body:
Daniel Kinahan appeared before the Special Criminal Court in Dublin on Sunday after being extradited from the United Arab Emirates, in what has been described as one of the most significant operations in Irish criminal justice history.

Kinahan, 49, was flown back to Ireland on a government jet that travelled to Dubai on Saturday. He was met at Casement Aerodrome by a Garda escort and formally charged with directing the activities of a criminal organisation between October 2015 and April 2017.

## A high-security operation

The Irish Prison Service had purchased a bulletproof and bombproof van to transport Kinahan to the courts in Dublin. A high-speed convoy of blacked-out police cars swept through the capital as one of the world's most wanted men was processed through the justice system.

Kinahan had been held in Dubai since his arrest in April on an Irish warrant for alleged serious organised crime offences. His attempts to fight extradition were unsuccessful. The US government had imposed sanctions on Kinahan and other family members in 2022, offering a reward of up to $5 million for information leading to their arrest.

The UAE and Irish Justice Ministers issued a joint statement calling Kinahan "one of the most high-profile individuals sought for prosecution in connection with transnational organised crime."

articles.headline: Man's body found in burning car in Portadown
articles.subtitle: Police and firefighters discovered a man's remains after being called to a car fire in the County Armagh town. A forensic investigation is under way.
articles.body:
A man has been pronounced dead at the scene of a car fire in Portadown, County Armagh, police have confirmed. Emergency services were called to Harford Street area in the early hours of Sunday, where they found a vehicle well alight.

Firefighters extinguished the blaze before the body of a man was discovered inside the car. Police have cordoned off the area and a forensic examination is under way. The Police Service of Northern Ireland has not yet released the identity of the deceased but said next of kin have been informed.

Detectives are treating the death as suspicious and are appealing for anyone who was in the Harford Street area around the time of the incident to come forward. A post-mortem examination is expected to determine the cause of death.

articles.headline: Harry Potter fans force diversion of UK-Ireland power link to avoid 'Dobby's grave'
articles.subtitle: Potter enthusiasts protested after a project manager suggested underwater cables would go beneath the grave of the beloved house-elf character in Freshwater West, Wales, prompting a route change.
articles.body:
Harry Potter fans have successfully lobbied to divert a major UK-Ireland power interconnector after expressing outrage that cables would pass beneath the site known as "Dobby's grave" at Freshwater West beach in Pembrokeshire, Wales.

The beach, which featured in the Harry Potter films as the location where Dobby the house-elf is buried, has become a pilgrimage site for fans who leave painted pebbles and socks — Dobby's emblem — at the spot. When the project manager mentioned in a BBC interview that cables would go under the area, fans mobilised quickly on social media.

## Route change confirmed

The energy companies behind the interconnector announced they would reroute the cables to avoid the memorial site. A spokesperson said the company had "listened to the community" and found an alternative route that would not disturb the area.

Local businesses in Pembrokeshire, where tourism has benefited significantly from Potter-themed visits, welcomed the decision. The grave has become one of Wales' most visited film locations since its appearance in "Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows: Part 1".

articles.headline: Most of sun to be eclipsed across island of Ireland on Wednesday
articles.subtitle: Skywatchers across Ireland will see a deep partial solar eclipse on Wednesday, followed by the peak of the Perseid meteor shower, in a week of celestial events.
articles.body:
Ireland is preparing for a "really exciting" partial solar eclipse on Wednesday, with astronomy enthusiasts across the island set to witness the moon cover a significant portion of the sun's disk. While the total eclipse path crosses mainland Spain, Ireland will experience a deep partial eclipse.

The partial eclipse will be visible across all of Ireland, with those in the west and south-west seeing a greater proportion of the sun obscured. The event coincides with the peak of the Perseid meteor shower, making for an extraordinary week for skywatchers.

## Viewing advice

Astronomers have urged the public to use proper solar viewing glasses and never look directly at the sun, even during the partial phase. Local astronomy groups are organising supervised viewing events across the country. Schools have been asked to incorporate the eclipse into their science lessons.

Experts note that Wednesday's event will be a warm-up for the total solar eclipse visible from Spain — including from Galicia — on the same day, which has drawn thousands of Irish tourists to travel to Spain for the full experience.

articles.headline: Fleadh Cheoil na hÉireann closes in Belfast after record-breaking week
articles.subtitle: The All-Ireland Fleadh, hosted in Belfast for the first time, exceeded its projected £53 million economic boost with visitor numbers surpassing one million.
articles.body:
The All-Ireland Fleadh Cheoil na hÉireann drew to a close in Belfast on Sunday after a record-breaking week that exceeded all expectations. The annual celebration of traditional Irish music, song and dance, hosted in Belfast for the first time, attracted more than one million visitors and generated an economic impact well above the projected £53 million.

Extended road closures that had been in place across the city centre were lifted early Monday morning. The festival featured more than 200 events, including competitions, concerts and street performances, with participants and visitors from across Ireland and the Irish diaspora worldwide.

## Cross-community success

Organisers hailed the event as "truly historic" for its cross-community participation. Belfast, a city still navigating its post-Troubles identity, saw Protestant and Catholic communities come together to celebrate a shared cultural heritage. The Taoiseach praised the "cross-community spirit" of the Fleadh, while local businesses reported their best trading week of the year.

The success has prompted discussions about making Belfast a regular host. Comhaltas Ceoltóirí Éireann, the organising body, said they would consider future bids from the city.

articles.headline: Netanyahu rejects Trump's 15-point plan for Gaza, conditions any withdrawal on total Hamas disarmament
articles.subtitle: Israel's prime minister says the military will not pull out of over 60% of Gaza until the militant group hands over its weapons 'genuinely and completely'.
articles.body:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has rejected the 15-point plan for Gaza pushed by the Trump administration, insisting that any Israeli withdrawal from the territory is conditional on the "total and authentic" disarmament of Hamas.

The plan, which the US had been promoting as a roadmap toward ending the current phase of the conflict, proposed a staged Israeli withdrawal from more than 60% of Gaza alongside security guarantees and reconstruction aid. Netanyahu's office said in a statement that Israel "will not accept any arrangement that leaves Hamas with military capabilities."

## A blow to US diplomacy

The rejection is a significant setback for US diplomatic efforts in the region and for President Trump personally, who had invested political capital in brokering a deal. US mediators had presented the framework as a compromise that would allow Israel to claim a military victory while providing Hamas with a political exit.

Netanyahu's stance puts him on a collision course not only with Washington but also with moderate Arab states that had been prepared to support the reconstruction plan. Meanwhile, the Israeli military continues operations in southern Gaza, and Palestinian civilian casualties continue to mount.

articles.headline: Typhoon Dolphin batters Japan's Okinawa before bearing down on eastern China
articles.subtitle: The powerful storm has cut power to at least 44,000 buildings, injured five people in Okinawa, and forced the evacuation of over a million people in China's Zhejiang province.
articles.body:
Typhoon Dolphin has swept through Japan's Okinawa island chain, leaving a trail of destruction before turning its sights toward mainland China, where authorities have evacuated more than one million people from coastal areas in Zhejiang province.

In Okinawa, the typhoon brought sustained winds of over 160 km/h, cutting power to at least 44,000 buildings and injuring five people. Schools and businesses were closed as residents hunkered down. The storm uprooted trees and caused significant damage to infrastructure on several of the southern Japanese islands.

## China braces for impact

China's meteorological agency has issued its highest-level red alert for Typhoon Dolphin, which is expected to make landfall near the port city of Ningbo later Monday. Authorities have suspended rail services, closed schools and tourist attractions, and deployed emergency response teams to the most vulnerable areas.

The typhoon is the most powerful to threaten China's eastern seaboard this year and comes as the region is already grappling with extreme weather events linked to climate change. The storm is expected to weaken as it moves inland but could still cause significant flooding and landslides.

articles.headline: Trump renews effort to fire Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook
articles.subtitle: The president is moving forward with a new attempt to remove the Fed official, continuing his assault on central bank independence despite a Supreme Court setback in June.
articles.body:
President Donald Trump is renewing his effort to fire Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook, keeping alive his assault on the central bank's independence even after the US Supreme Court dealt him a significant setback in June, according to a letter seen by Reuters.

The new attempt comes after the Supreme Court ruled that Trump could not remove Cook without cause. The White House is now arguing that new grounds for removal have emerged, though the specifics of the claim remain unclear.

## Market reaction

Financial markets reacted nervously to the news, with the dollar weakening slightly and Treasury yields edging higher as traders priced in a greater risk of political interference in monetary policy. The Fed has maintained interest rates at current levels amid persistent inflation, a stance that Trump has publicly criticised.

Fed Chair Jerome Powell declined to comment on the matter during a scheduled appearance, but the central bank has previously defended its governors' independence as essential to credible monetary policy. Cook herself has not publicly responded to the renewed attempt to remove her.

articles.headline: State of emergency declared as fast-moving Canadian wildfire doubles in size
articles.subtitle: British Columbia declares a state of emergency as 20,000 people flee fast-moving wildfires that have doubled in size, with hot and dry conditions hampering firefighting efforts.
articles.body:
British Columbia declared a state of emergency on Sunday as a fast-moving wildfire doubled in size, forcing approximately 20,000 people to flee their homes in the Okanagan region. The wildfire, fuelled by extreme heat and dry conditions that have persisted through the summer, has consumed thousands of hectares of forest and threatened several communities.

Evacuation orders were issued for multiple towns and neighbourhoods, with residents told to leave immediately as the fire front advanced more rapidly than anticipated. Emergency shelters have been set up in nearby cities, and the Canadian military has been deployed to support firefighting efforts.

## A worsening fire season

Canada is experiencing one of its worst wildfire seasons on record, with millions of hectares already burned across the country. Climate scientists point to a combination of prolonged drought, higher-than-average temperatures and changes in forest management as contributing factors.

The British Columbia government has appealed for federal assistance, and Prime Minister Andy Burnham's government has promised to make additional resources available. Air quality warnings are in effect across a wide area, with smoke drifting hundreds of kilometres from the fire zones.

articles.headline: Jorge Messi, Lionel Messi's father and longtime agent, dies at 68
articles.subtitle: The death of Jorge Messi, the architect behind his son's legendary career and the figure who signed the famous napkin contract with Barcelona, has sparked an outpouring of tributes.
articles.body:
Jorge Messi, the father and longtime agent of football legend Lionel Messi, has died at the age of 68 following a long illness. His death was confirmed by family sources in Rosario, Argentina.

Jorge Messi was instrumental in managing his son's career from its earliest days. He famously negotiated Lionel's first contract with FC Barcelona, a deal famously scrawled on a napkin in a restaurant when the young prodigy's family relocated from Argentina to Catalonia to pursue his dream at La Masia.

## A complex legacy

While Jorge Messi helped build one of the most successful careers in sporting history — guiding his son to eight Ballon d'Or awards and a World Cup victory — their relationship with Barcelona became strained in later years. The family's financial demands were cited as a factor in Lionel Messi's emotional departure from the club in 2021.

Tributes have poured in from across the football world, with former teammates, clubs and rivals offering condolences. Lionel Messi has not yet made a public statement, but those close to the family say he is devastated by the loss.

articles.headline: Cloudflare launches Kitesurf, a browser built entirely for AI agents
articles.subtitle: The cloud-hosted browser, built from scratch in Rust, uses 3-7x less memory than Chromium for automation tasks and shifts focus from human interfaces to agent infrastructure.
articles.body:
Cloudflare has launched Kitesurf, a cloud-hosted browser designed specifically for AI agents rather than human users. Built from scratch in Rust and compiled to WebAssembly, Kitesurf runs entirely within Cloudflare's network and is available in free beta through the Browser Run service on Cloudflare Workers.

The browser strips away everything a human needs — tabs, extensions, GPU-accelerated rendering, pixel-perfect anti-aliasing — and keeps only what an AI agent requires: the ability to navigate websites, take screenshots, extract HTML and fill out forms. Cloudflare claims the browser uses three to seven times less memory than Chromium for common automation tasks.

## Built for the agent era

Cloudflare built Kitesurf in 12 weeks using components including Blitz, Firefox's Stylo CSS engine, and the Boa JavaScript engine. The company says it addresses the key bottlenecks agent developers face: context handling, token costs, scalability and protection against prompt injection attacks.

"Humans will be a rounding error on the internet," a Cloudflare executive said, predicting machine-generated traffic will surge 1,000 times in five years. Kitesurf is Cloudflare's third major agent-related launch in "Agents Week," following the @cloudflare/computer workspace and the Cloudflare OS platform.

articles.headline: Framework notifies all customers of data breach after security incident
articles.subtitle: The computer maker confirmed that an unauthorised party accessed customer data, including names, email addresses and shipping information, in a breach affecting its entire customer base.
articles.body:
Framework, the modular laptop manufacturer, has notified all of its customers of a data breach after an unauthorised party gained access to its systems. The company confirmed that the breach exposed customer names, email addresses, shipping addresses and order histories.

In an email to customers, Framework said it had identified the security incident and taken immediate steps to contain it, including rotating credentials and engaging external cybersecurity experts. The company said it did not believe financial information was compromised, as it uses third-party payment processors.

## Industry-wide scrutiny

The Framework breach comes amid heightened scrutiny of hardware supply chain security. The company, known for its repairable, upgradeable laptops, has a loyal customer base that has responded with a mixture of concern and sympathy.

Framework has advised customers to be vigilant against phishing attempts that may use the exposed data, and has committed to implementing additional security measures including mandatory two-factor authentication for all accounts.

articles.headline: New Mexico court orders Meta to pay additional $567M in child safety case
articles.subtitle: The ruling adds to Meta's mounting legal liabilities over allegations that its platforms failed to protect minors from predation and harmful content.
articles.body:
A New Mexico court has ordered Meta to pay an additional $567 million in damages in a child safety case, adding to the social media giant's growing legal exposure over the treatment of minors on its platforms. The ruling stems from a lawsuit alleging that Meta's platforms, including Instagram and Facebook, failed to protect underage users from sexual exploitation and harmful content.

The company has said it will appeal the decision. Meta has faced a wave of similar lawsuits from states and individuals across the US, with plaintiffs arguing that the company prioritised engagement over child safety. The company has defended its safety measures and pointed to features it has introduced including default private accounts for minors.

## Regulatory pressure mounts

The New Mexico ruling comes amid broader regulatory pressure on social media companies over child safety. The EU's Digital Services Act has already forced platforms to implement more robust age verification and content moderation systems, while the UK's Online Safety Act imposes similar requirements.

Meta has invested heavily in safety infrastructure in recent years, but critics argue these efforts have been insufficient to address the scale of the problem.

articles.headline: Ransomware gangs target 40-something IT managers instead of CEOs
articles.subtitle: Attackers have shifted tactics, bypassing C-suite executives and going straight for mid-career IT staff who hold the keys to network access and system credentials.
articles.body:
Ransomware gangs are changing their tactics, bypassing chief executives and targeting 40-something IT managers who are more likely to hold the keys to critical network access, according to cybersecurity researchers. The shift reflects a sophisticated understanding of corporate hierarchies and who actually has the credentials to unlock systems.

Analysis of recent ransomware campaigns shows attackers are using social engineering and spear-phishing to identify and target IT operations staff in their forties — the demographic most likely to have accumulated significant technical privileges over a career without the same security awareness training as C-suite executives.

## The human factor

The trend highlights a persistent vulnerability in enterprise security: the gap between technical access and security awareness. While CEOs and CFOs receive regular phishing simulations and incident response training, the engineers and system administrators who manage day-to-day network operations are often overlooked.

Security experts recommend organisations extend their security awareness programmes to all technical staff, implement strict access controls based on the principle of least privilege, and ensure that no single individual has the ability to approve and execute critical system changes without oversight.

articles.headline: OpenAI rolls out major ChatGPT upgrade with GPT-5.6 Sol for Plus and Pro users
articles.subtitle: The update brings a more reliable version of the model to paying customers, while free users receive unlimited text chats with a lighter GPT-5.6 Luna variant.
articles.body:
OpenAI has begun rolling out a significant upgrade to ChatGPT, with Plus and Pro subscribers receiving GPT-5.6 Sol — described by the company as its most reliable model yet. Free users are also getting an upgrade: unlimited text chats with GPT-5.6 Luna, a lighter variant that retains much of the improved performance.

The Sol model represents a focus on consistency and reliability over raw capability. OpenAI's research suggests that users value predictable, trustworthy outputs over occasional flashes of brilliance, and the training regime for Sol was weighted heavily toward reducing hallucinations and improving factual accuracy.

## A two-tier strategy

The dual-model approach signals OpenAI's evolving strategy for its consumer product. Luna, available to free users, removes the previous message caps and provides a capable experience, while Sol monetises the highest-quality outputs. The company has not disclosed pricing changes for the Plus subscription.

The rollout comes as competition in the consumer AI space intensifies, with Anthropic, Google and a growing number of open-source models vying for users. The upgrade also follows several high-profile incidents involving AI model safety, and OpenAI emphasised that Sol has undergone extensive safety testing before release.

articles.headline: AI agents to get a common language as tech giants standardise 'Agent Plugins 1.0'
articles.subtitle: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google and others have agreed on a write-once-run-anywhere container standard for passing tools and skills across different AI agent platforms.
articles.body:
Major AI companies including Anthropic, OpenAI and Google have agreed on a common standard for AI agent interoperability, announcing Agent Plugins 1.0. The specification defines a write-once-run-anywhere container format that allows tools, skills and capabilities to be shared across different agent platforms.

The standard addresses one of the fundamental challenges of the emerging agent ecosystem: fragmentation. Currently, a tool built for one platform's agent — say, a Claude skill — requires significant rework to function on ChatGPT or Gemini. Agent Plugins 1.0 aims to make that frictionless.

## A fragmented landscape

The initiative reflects a recognition that no single company will dominate the agent ecosystem, and that interoperability is essential for the industry to scale. The standard covers authentication, capability discovery, execution patterns and safety constraints.

Critics note that similar promises of standardisation have fallen short in the past — the "write once, run anywhere" slogan was famously associated with Java applets, which never fully delivered. However, the backing of the three largest AI companies gives Agent Plugins 1.0 a better chance of adoption than previous efforts.

articles.headline: AI struggles to patch software vulnerabilities without human supervision
articles.subtitle: Research shows autonomous AI agents tasked with fixing security flaws often fail to fully remediate the issues, with fixes that look correct but leave underlying vulnerabilities unaddressed.
articles.body:
Autonomous AI agents tasked with patching software vulnerabilities frequently fail to fully remediate the underlying issues, according to new research. While the AI-generated patches often appear correct at first glance, a significant proportion leave the original flaw partially or entirely unaddressed.

The finding is significant as companies increasingly deploy AI coding agents to automate security remediation. The research tested several leading models on a standardised set of vulnerabilities and found that while the agents were good at producing plausible-looking diffs, they often missed edge cases or applied superficial fixes.

## The supervision gap

A related study on human oversight of AI agents found that human reviewers missed approximately one in three dangerous requests made to AI coding agents — including requests that would leak credentials or modify Kubernetes configurations. The combination of imperfect AI patches and imperfect human supervision creates a security gap that researchers say needs urgent attention.

The findings have prompted calls for more rigorous testing frameworks for AI-generated code, and for organisations to maintain traditional security review processes alongside AI-assisted development workflows.

articles.headline: Beijing launches cybersecurity review into Palo Alto Networks' China products
articles.subtitle: China's cyberspace administration has initiated an investigation into the US cybersecurity firm's products, mirroring the process that preceded the 2023 ban on Micron chips.
articles.body:
China has launched a cybersecurity review of Palo Alto Networks' products sold in the country, the Chinese cyberspace administration announced. The investigation follows the same procedural path as the 2023 review that led to a ban on Micron Technology's chips.

Beijing did not specify the reasons for the review, which will examine whether Palo Alto Networks' products pose a national security risk. The company is one of the largest US cybersecurity firms operating in China, providing network security and threat detection services to major Chinese enterprises and government agencies.

## Tit-for-tat tech tensions

The review appears to be the latest salvo in ongoing technology tensions between the US and China. Washington has increasingly restricted Chinese technology imports, including semiconductor equipment and AI models, citing national security concerns. Beijing's move against Palo Alto Networks may be a retaliatory measure.

Palo Alto Networks said in a statement that it would cooperate fully with the review. The company's shares dipped on the news. Industry analysts warn that a potential ban would disrupt cybersecurity defences at Chinese institutions that rely on Palo Alto's products.
